question.text: Under the NPS overseas-distribution fee rules, what is the correct onboarding-fee cap when a retirement adviser sources applications from prospects outside India?

answer.text: Up to US$8 when the overseas-sourced application is sent to a Point of Presence in India or opened online, and up to US$2 when it is submitted to a registered PoP branch in the overseas territory
Up to US$2 when an overseas-sourced application is sent to an Indian Point of Presence
Up to US$8 in every case where the application is sourced in the overseas territory, regardless of where it is submitted
No onboarding fee is allowed for prospects outside India

explanation.text: The Logic: The NPS overseas-distribution fee structure is split by the submission channel. When an overseas-sourced application is sent to a Point of Presence in India or opened online, the cap is up to US$8. When it is submitted to a registered PoP branch in that overseas territory, the cap is up to US$2. A separate cap of up to US$1 per transaction applies to each subsequent overseas service request. The Trap: Attaching US$2 to the Indian-PoP route reverses the two caps. A flat US$8 in every case ignores the lower cap that applies when the PoP's overseas branch handles the submission. Claiming no fee is allowed contradicts the rule entirely. Note: A separate cap of up to US$1 per transaction applies to each subsequent overseas service request, distinct from the US$8 and US$2 onboarding caps tied to the submission channel.
